name: Domaine Huet Vouvray Moelleux 1ère Trie Le Mont 2015
text:
## Domaine Huet Vouvray Moelleux 1ère Trie Le Mont 2015

**The story.** [Domaine Huet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domaine_Huet) in [Vouvray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vouvray), on the [Loire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loire) just east of [Tours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tours) ([see it from above](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Domaine+Huet,+Vouvray,+France&t=k)), is considered the most celebrated wine producer of the [Loire Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loire_Valley_%28wine%29) ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domaine_Huet)). It was founded in 1928 by Victor Huet and his son Gaston, and makes only [Chenin Blanc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chenin_blanc), in every style from sparkling to dry to lusciously sweet. When Gaston Huet died in 2002, the estate had to be sold to pay French inheritance taxes. In 2003 it was bought by the Hwang family, who also own the [Tokaji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokaji) estate Királyudvar in Hungary. Gaston's son-in-law Noël Pinguet stayed on as winemaker until February 2012 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domaine_Huet)).

**The vineyards.** Huet farms 30 hectares [biodynamically](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biodynamic_agriculture), in three famous vineyards: [Le Haut-Lieu](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Le+Haut-Lieu,+Vouvray,+France&t=k) (15 hectares), [Le Clos du Bourg](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Clos+du+Bourg,+Vouvray,+France&t=k) (6 hectares, bought in 1953) and [Le Mont](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Le+Mont,+Vouvray,+France&t=k) (9 hectares, bought in 1957) ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domaine_Huet)). Vouvray's vineyards sit on a plateau above the river, on gravel and clay over [tuffeau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuffeau_stone), the soft white limestone used to build the châteaux of the Loire ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vouvray_%28wine%29)). The German merchant Living Wines describes Le Mont as the site that brings smoky, dark and spicy notes to Vouvray, with a stony minerality ([Living Wines](https://www.lebendigeweine.de/en/le-mont-moelleux-1ere-trie-2015-huet/)).

**The wine: Moelleux 1ère Trie.** "Moelleux" means sweet, and "Première Trie" means "first selection". In warm years, the pickers go through the vineyard several times ("tries"), hand-picking only the ripest berries each time, often grapes touched by [noble rot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noble_rot) ([Botrytis cinerea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Botrytis_cinerea)), which concentrates sugar and flavour. Vouvray's harvest is often the last in France, sometimes running into November ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vouvray_%28wine%29)). The 1ère Trie is the most concentrated of these selections: in effect, the estate's sweetest, richest wine from that vineyard in that year.

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [Loire Valley vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/loire-valley) calls 2015 very promising across the region, with the same warm, dry summer that many other French regions enjoyed. Touraine, Vouvray's district, had very low yields but excellent quality, and Chenin Blanc did well, with "the potential to make good wine at all sweetness levels". Living Wines notes that of Huet's three 1ère Trie wines in 2015, Le Mont was typically the most closed when young ([Living Wines](https://www.lebendigeweine.de/en/le-mont-moelleux-1ere-trie-2015-huet/)).

**What the critics say for 2015.** As listed by [Farr Vintners](https://farrvintners.com/wine.php?wine=44181):
- **[Wine Advocate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wine_Advocate): 98** (Stephan Reinhardt, October 2016). Super clear, ripe and aromatic, highly elegant, with lovely flinty flavours; intense and concentrated, with great finesse and vitality, perfectly balanced, with persistent grip and salinity. Drink 2020 to 2050.
- **[Wine Spectator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wine_Spectator): 95** (James Molesworth, January 2016). Ripe and energetic: unctuous [quince](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quince), melon, fig and pear, with green tea, honeysuckle and [cardamom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardamom); a long, lush finish with "latent, rippling minerality". "A beauty." Drink through 2035.
- **Christoph Raffelt, [Living Wines](https://www.lebendigeweine.de/en/le-mont-moelleux-1ere-trie-2015-huet/)** (tasting note, no score). Deep gold; pear, [galangal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galangal) and [saffron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saffron) spice with brioche; dark, spicy and smoky, with stony minerality, stone fruit and notes of hay, chamomile and elderberry. Above all, the acidity "takes the leading role", balancing the lavish sweetness.
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 94.2** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is eleven years old, still young for a great sweet Vouvray. Wine Advocate's window runs to 2050, and Wikipedia notes that top Vouvray from good vintages can age for decades, more commonly peaking around 40 years and occasionally lasting a century ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vouvray_%28wine%29)). It's lovely now, but there is no hurry at all: this is a bottle that can be passed down.

**Serving.** Serve it well chilled but not ice-cold, about 10 to 12°C, in a white-wine glass. No need to decant. A half-glass goes a long way: it is rich and sweet, but the high natural acidity of Chenin Blanc keeps it fresh rather than cloying ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vouvray_%28wine%29)).

**Food.** Christoph Raffelt suggests [Norway lobster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nephrops_norvegicus) with lobster foam and [tarragon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarragon), a [mille-feuille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mille-feuille) of wild strawberries and yellow peach, or a baked chocolate ganache with spiced hazelnuts and orange oil ([Living Wines](https://www.lebendigeweine.de/en/le-mont-moelleux-1ere-trie-2015-huet/)). My picks: [foie gras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foie_gras), a blue cheese such as [Roquefort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roquefort), a [tarte Tatin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarte_Tatin), or simply on its own after dinner.

**Value and where to buy.** None of the three stores on this site lists Huet's sweet wines. Huet's sweet 1ère Trie wines turn up with fine-wine merchants such as [Farr Vintners](https://farrvintners.com/wine.php?wine=44181) and at auction. In my view, a 98-point sweet wine that can last half a century is excellent value next to the great Sauternes.

**From the history books**
- **Monks, Dutch merchants and caves.** Vines have grown in Vouvray since at least the Middle Ages, when the Church kept vineyards at local monasteries. In the 16th and 17th centuries, Dutch merchants planted vineyards to supply London, Paris and Rotterdam. The cellars are caves dug out when the [tuffeau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuffeau_stone) stone was quarried to build the châteaux of the Loire ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vouvray_%28wine%29)).
- **Pineau de la Loire.** [Chenin Blanc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chenin_blanc), known locally as Pineau de la Loire, probably originated in Anjou around the 9th century before moving upriver to Vouvray. Vouvray became an appellation in 1936, the same year as Châteauneuf-du-Pape ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vouvray_%28wine%29)).
- **Bought in 1957.** Gaston Huet bought the Le Mont vineyard in 1957, after Le Clos du Bourg in 1953 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domaine_Huet)).
- **Sold for the taxman.** When Gaston Huet died in 2002, French inheritance tax forced the sale of the estate; the Hwang family bought it in 2003 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domaine_Huet)).

**Curious details**
- **One of the greatest wines ever made.** In 2005 [Decanter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decanter_%28magazine%29) listed its 100 greatest wines ever made. A 1947 Huet ranked sixth, the second-highest white wine on the list after the 1921 [Château d'Yquem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teau_d'Yquem) ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domaine_Huet)).
- **Christie's.** Huet is the only Loire producer to have headlined an auction at [Christie's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christie's) ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domaine_Huet)).
- **Sweet or dry depends on the weather.** In Vouvray the vintage decides the style: cool years make mostly dry and sparkling wine, warm years allow sweet moelleux like this one ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vouvray_%28wine%29)).
- **The river mists.** Small rivers that feed the Loire near Vouvray, such as the [Cisse](https://www.google.com/maps?q=La+Cisse,+Vouvray,+France&t=k) and the Brenne, help create the damp autumn mornings that encourage noble rot ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vouvray_%28wine%29)).
